findings.claim: usePlaybackClock.ts no longer reads the core shared clock (`@/lib/mediaClock`, `subscribeMediaClock`/`getMediaClockSnapshot`). It now runs its own 250 ms setInterval on the controller. When a controller getter throws, its catch returns IDLE_PLAYBACK, which is time 0 and duration 0, instead of keeping the last good reading as the shared clock does.
findings.impact: Each shown Scenes section adds a second poller per controller, running at 250 ms even while paused, where the shared clock idles at 1000 ms. If a controller getter throws in a sample, the time reads as 0 for that sample: the playing outline moves to tile 0, and while following the list scrolls to row 0 and then back on the next sample. The old path could not produce time 0 this way, because getMediaClockSnapshot never throws and holds the last good snapshot. No test covers a controller that throws. The touch-point list says only 'hooks; a follow hook added' and does not mention the clock source changing.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/frontend/ScenesSection/hooks/usePlaybackClock.ts:40-50 (readSnapshot calls controller getters directly, and catch returns IDLE_PLAYBACK) and :96-101 (setInterval 250). frontend/src/lib/mediaClock.ts:1-8 says to poll 'exactly once per controller, here, instead of once per consumer'. mediaClock.ts:115-125 holds the last good reading on a throw ('The YouTube player throws while it swaps media'). The revised SPEC-ADDON-089 I2 says the marker and outline 'follow the shared media clock'.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. I could not confirm that a controller getter throws in normal use: YouTubeEmbed.tsx shows no explicit throw. The only evidence is the comment in mediaClock.ts.

bucket_proposal.reason: In normal operation the polled values match the shared clock's values, so a user-visible breach of SPEC-ADDON-089 I2 depends on a getter throw I could not confirm. The finding is mainly that the code departs from the documented single-poller design and the clock is not named among the touch points.

findings.proposed_fix: Keep subscribing to the shared clock, and add a separate check for paused seeks if needed, or hold the last good reading on a throw instead of returning IDLE_PLAYBACK.

findings.claim: In flow form the card box (cardBoxRef) is always rendered while expanded, with padding and an opaque background. viewportOf therefore ends the visible area at the card box's top whenever the box has any height, including when neither the card nor the placeholder is drawn.
findings.impact: On the phone sheet with no Visual Index (policy off, 404, not eligible, or no labelled scene), an empty opaque strip of about 0.875rem + 0.5rem + the safe-area inset stays pinned at the bottom of the scroller and covers tiles. The visible area, and with it following, wholly-visible checks, the band, the top row and picture requests, ends above the scroller's bottom. The flow-form tests all use a Visual Index with a card, so no test would fail.
findings.evidence: ScenesSectionPresenter.tsx:371-381 renders the cardBoxRef div whenever view === "expanded", with `sticky ... pt-3.5 pb-[calc(env(safe-area-inset-bottom)+0.5rem)] bg-bg-card` in flow form, whatever the children are. sceneList.ts viewportOf: `bottom = card && card.height > 0 ? card.top : scroller bottom`. The padding keeps card.height above 0 when the box is empty. The flow e2e fixture (ScenesFlowArrangement) always serves SCENES_LONG_VISUAL_INDEX with a scene, and scenes-scroll-list.spec.ts uses the default vi.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Mentally: open #scenes-flow with policy off or the visual-index stub returning 404. The cardBox renders empty with padding, so getBoundingClientRect().height > 0 and viewportOf.bottom = cardBox.top, which is above the scroller's client bottom.

bucket_proposal.reason: I11 (acceptance) requires that in flow form, when neither the card nor the placeholder is drawn, the visible area ends at the scroller's bottom.

findings.proposed_fix: Render the sticky card box in flow form only when the placeholder or a scene card is drawn, or have viewportOf ignore the box when it has no card or placeholder child.

potential_unspecified_behavior: The Container's reset layout effect depends on `mediaController != null`, and useSceneList's show effect depends on `hasPlayback`. A controller appearing while the section is shown therefore removes the ruler point and sets following again, even after a reader's scroll. The spec lists the controller appearing only as a placement event, not as an event that sets following or removes the ruler point.
A mouse press with the right button (button 2) on the ruler sets the ruler point. Only the middle button is excluded.
usePlaybackClock still computes isJump and calls an onJump the Container now passes as a noop: dead logic.
regression_risks: The section's own 250 ms poller replaces the shared media clock (TP-2), changing the timing and the behaviour on a getter throw.
In flow form with no Visual Index, an empty pinned strip at the sheet's bottom shrinks the visible area (F-1).
Every tile is mounted (up to max_frames). Clock ticks rely on SceneTile memoisation with stable callbacks.
test_coverage: The jsdom suites (ScenesSectionScrollList, RulerMap, Reload) cover following, the chip, the ruler point's lifetime, the band, the 150 ms picture settle and pointercancel restore on a stubbed layout.
The e2e flow-form cases always have a scene card, so I11's no-card visible-area clause is untested (F-1).
No test makes a controller getter throw or checks that the section uses the shared media clock (TP-2).
not_verified: I did not run any test, unit or e2e; the review is reading only.
